title: Engram process tree holds its terminated mutex across bounded kill and absence probes
outcome: EngramProcessTree does not hold its terminated mutex while sleeping or probing. confirmed_after_reap copies the TerminalGroupSignal out of the guard before it runs the post-reap absence probe. terminate() records its outcome without keeping the lock held across kill_before_reap's bounded leader-exit look and kill_child_process's waits. Either that, or the bound is documented as accepted. A concurrent request_termination, whether from a successor in process_for_until or from Drop, no longer overruns its own deadline by up to about 250-350 ms.
acceptance: confirmed_after_reap and terminate() in src/engram_host_adapter.rs do not hold the terminated mutex across the bounded leader-exit look, the post-reap absence probe or the kill waits; or the bound is documented at the lock and the coordinator has concurred on that choice in a note
the change is reviewed and gated under the standing rule
